A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same PolyInter research and contain readable main text, equations, figures, tables and supplementary material. Retained content can be reliably matched across appendix reordering and renumbering.

before.justification: V1 reports original collaborative detection results on OPV2V and V2XSet, including baseline comparisons, component ablations, parameter-efficiency experiments and qualitative evaluations.

after.justification: V2 retains these original results and adds DAIR-V2X evaluations, LiDAR–camera comparisons and loss-function ablations.

M1.justification: Section 3 retains the same two-phase interpreter, channel selection, spatial attention, general and specific prompts, losses and low-rank adaptation. The camera experiments do not document a modification to PolyInter's procedure or architecture.

E1.justification: V2 adds real-world DAIR-V2X evaluation and LiDAR–camera collaboration scenarios using ResNet and EfficientNet neighbors. These substantially extend the represented environments and input modalities. OPV2V and V2XSet were already evaluated in v1.

E2.justification: PnPDA and MPDA remain the evaluated interpreter comparators, with F-cooper and CoBEVT as fusion choices. The added multimodal and DAIR-V2X comparisons extend this same set; existing comparisons retain their participants.

E3.justification: V2 specifies new multimodal training/evaluation configurations: pp8-pp4-EfficientNet followed by adaptation to ResNet, and pp8-vn4-ResNet followed by adaptation to EfficientNet. Existing LiDAR configurations, AP metrics, evaluation range and two-phase evaluation procedure remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Supplementary Table 2 adds a focused ablation removing style, adversarial and single-agent losses separately across three encoder pairings. This extends the existing module, prompt-initialization and rank analyses with direct checks of the auxiliary training objectives.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. The new results continue the existing point-estimate reporting practice.

E6.justification: V2 adds multimodal, DAIR-V2X and loss-ablation result tables. For example, supplementary Table 5 reports DAIR-V2X pp8-pp4 AP@0.5/AP@0.7 with CoBEVT of 66.8/39.9 for PolyInter, 62.9/34.4 for PnPDA and 65.0/35.1 for MPDA. These are new evaluation results; matched pre-existing numerical results remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Equations (1)–(11), the mathematical loss definitions and the low-rank parameter-count derivations remain unchanged. No theorems, proofs or formal assumptions are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and conclusion retain the same claims about a single extensible interpreter, channel/spatial alignment and prompt-based adaptation. The headline claims of up to 11.1% improvement and adaptation using 1.4% of parameters are unchanged.

C2.justification: Section 3.3 changes the style-loss rationale from preventing excessive feature concentration or dispersion to preventing dependence on a single agent. It also more strongly describes adversarial training as excluding agent-specific semantics and preserving exclusively shared semantics, without changing the mathematical objective.

D1.justification: V2 adds a code-availability statement and repository address in the abstract. Existing prompt dimensions, loss weights, resizer specifications and parameter counts remain unchanged. The PDFs establish the new access information, but do not establish repository completeness or usability.

R1.justification: V2 adds references for ResNet, EfficientNet and DAIR-V2X to support the new experiments. The related-work discussion and positioning against one-stage and two-stage interpreters remain substantively unchanged; most citation changes are renumbering.

P1.justification: The abstract and selected method, experimental and qualitative paragraphs are tightened. The supplement is reorganized into more specific sections, and corresponding-author markers and a funding acknowledgement are added. The main narrative and section sequence remain largely intact.

P2.justification: Three supplementary tables are added using the existing presentation style, while retained tables and the supplementary figure are rearranged. Figure 3 gains channel labels. Figure 6 is reduced from six panels to four feature panels; prompt visualizations remain in supplementary Figure 1.

improvement.justification: V2 substantially strengthens validation by addressing v1's restriction to simulated, LiDAR-only evaluations through real-world DAIR-V2X and LiDAR–camera tests. The loss ablations also test previously unisolated training terms, while prior evidence is retained. Sparse documentation of the added experiments and absent uncertainty estimates limit the conclusions, but the gains in evidence for practical applicability are substantial.
